findings.title: Workflow-reminder cancellation is fire-and-forget and may never persist
findings.body: updatedBookings.forEach calls the now-async deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder without returning or awaiting them (same pattern in handleNewBooking reschedule and bookings.requestReschedule). deleteScheduledEmailReminder performs the prisma update that sets cancelled=true inside that unawaited promise, and the previous implementation's awaited prisma deleteMany was removed. The handler can finish/return (and a serverless invocation can freeze) before the update runs, and errors are only swallowed by the callee's catch, so a cancelled booking can keep an active SendGrid/Twilio reminder and the email/SMS is still sent.

findings.title: One failing SendGrid cancellation aborts cancellation of all remaining reminders
findings.body: The for loop awaits client.request for each reminder inside a single try/catch, and the prisma deletes are only executed via Promise.all after the loop completes. If any one request throws (e.g. a null/invalid referenceId, an already-handled batch, or a transient SendGrid error), the catch is taken immediately: reminders later in the list are never cancelled, and even reminders already successfully cancelled at SendGrid are never deleted from the DB. Because the failing reminder stays first-class on the next cron run, it can repeatedly block/poison all other pending cancellations and those emails will be sent at their scheduled time. Each reminder needs per-item error isolation and deletion.

findings.title: immediateDelete path loses the cancellation if SendGrid rejects it, with no deferred retry
findings.body: When immediateDelete is true (used for rescheduled bookings in handleNewBooking and for deleted workflows/steps in workflows.tsx) the function POSTs status=cancel to SendGrid and returns without deleting the WorkflowReminder row or setting cancelled=true. If that POST fails - e.g. the very 100-pending-cancellations limit this PR is meant to work around - the internal catch only logs it, so the DB still shows a normal scheduled reminder, the scheduleEmailReminders cron (which only acts on cancelled=true rows) will never retry it, and SendGrid will send the reminder for the rescheduled/deleted booking. The immediate path should fall back to marking the row cancelled on failure (and should remove/mark the row on success, since rescheduled bookings are not cascade-deleted).

findings.title: Deferred cancellation window lets imminently-due reminders be sent after cancellation
findings.body: Non-immediate cancellations only set cancelled=true; the email is only actually cancelled by this cron, which runs periodically (per PR description every 15 minutes) and picks up rows whose scheduledDate is within the next hour. If a booking is cancelled/rescheduled (via the non-immediate paths) shortly before a reminder's scheduledDate - e.g. 5 minutes before a 24h-before reminder fires - and the next cron run lands after that date, SendGrid dispatches the email before it is ever cancelled; the cron's first deleteMany then just deletes the past-due row. Cancellation needs an immediate SendGrid cancel when the scheduled time is near (or a much tighter guarantee), not purely deferred handling.
